loot: Zerith-Ka's gifts: each party member receives a Threadwalker's Focus — a small crystal tuned to their psychic frequency that grants advantage on saves against planar dissonance effects (this stacks with the Warden's Sigil if they found one); Zerith-Ka also offers to attune each character's primary weapon with a Planar Edge enchantment — the weapon deals an additional 1d4 force damage against creatures not native to the plane the wielder is currently on (this lasts for the duration of the scenario)

Knowledge: complete briefing on the Convergence, the Confluence, Threadwalking, and the Citadel's situation; this information provides advantage on Arcana checks related to planar phenomena for the remainder of the scenario

The silver compass is confirmed as a Warden's Compass — an artifact that always points toward the nearest Confluence fragment and grows warmer as the bearer approaches; Zerith-Ka reveals it has additional functions that will unlock as the party's Threadwalker abilities develop (future scenario hooks)

scenes.name: Shadows Within
scenes.description: While the party settles into the Citadel and prepares for the mission to seal the Convergence Wound, threats emerge from within. Githyanki infiltrators have breached the failing psychic defenses and are planting psionic charges on the Citadel's structural crystal, accelerating its collapse to create openings for Captain Kra'zith's assault force. Simultaneously, the warden Kael-Thun's secret negotiations with the githyanki create an atmosphere of suspicion and unease. The party must investigate strange sounds, discover the sabotage, root out the infiltrators, and decide what to do about Kael-Thun — whose motivations are not as simple as treachery. This scene combines investigation, social interaction, and a close-quarters combat encounter in the Citadel's damaged corridors.
scenes.readAloud: You are woken from meditation — or whatever passes for sleep in the Astral — by a sound that should not exist in a fortress of psychic crystal: a grinding, cracking noise, like ice breaking on a winter lake, followed by a tremor that shakes your chamber and sends dust — crystal dust, glittering and sharp — sifting down from the ceiling. The sound stops. The tremor fades. And in the silence that follows, you hear something else: footsteps. Not the soft, deliberate tread of githzerai wardens but something quicker, harder, moving with purpose through the corridor outside your quarters. Then a voice — barely audible, speaking a language that is not Common and not Gith but something between them, hissed and urgent. Then silence again. Outside your door, the corridor is empty. But on the crystal floor, visible in the wall's ambient glow, is a scuff mark — a boot print in crystal dust, pointing deeper into the Citadel toward the damaged sections. And on the wall beside your door, a hairline crack that was not there when you went to sleep has widened into a fracture the length of your arm, dark and deep and radiating cold.

skillChecks.success: Following the boot prints and examining the new crack, the character identifies the damage as deliberate sabotage — the crack was not caused by convergence stress but by a concentrated psionic charge placed against the crystal at its weakest point. The charge residue is visible as a faint purple stain on the crystal surface. Someone is methodically weakening the Citadel's structure.
skillChecks.failure: The crack appears to be convergence damage — just another sign of the Citadel's deterioration. The boot prints could belong to a warden on patrol.

skillChecks.success: The character follows the tracks silently through the damaged corridors and catches the githyanki infiltrators in the act of planting another psionic charge. The party has surprise and can observe or attack from an advantageous position.
skillChecks.failure: The character makes noise in the damaged corridor — a crystal shard crunches underfoot, or a loose piece of wall shifts. The infiltrators are alerted and prepare an ambush of their own.

skillChecks.success: The character notices that one section of the corridor wall — an area that should be solid crystal — is slightly different in color and texture: it is a psychic illusion concealing the gap in the defenses through which the infiltrators entered. Dispelling the illusion (DC 14 Arcana or Dispel Magic) reveals a hole in the psychic ward just large enough for a Medium creature to squeeze through.
skillChecks.failure: The walls appear intact. The character does not notice the concealed breach.

skillChecks.success: During any interaction with Kael-Thun — in the corridors, at meals, during warden briefings — the character notices his behavior: nervous glances toward the eastern wing, flinching at mentions of Captain Kra'zith, and a tendency to argue for evacuation rather than defense. He is hiding something, and it weighs on him. A direct, compassionate confrontation (DC 14 Persuasion) causes him to break down and confess his secret negotiations.
skillChecks.failure: Kael-Thun appears to be a stressed but loyal warden. Nothing unusual about his behavior stands out.

skillChecks.success: Kael-Thun confesses everything: he has been in psychic contact with a githyanki intermediary, negotiating safe passage for the surviving wardens in exchange for allowing Kra'zith's forces to loot the Citadel's archives. He is not a traitor in his own mind — he genuinely believes the Citadel will fall and is trying to save lives. He weeps as he confesses. 'Zerith-Ka will fight to the last. She will die here. And she will take all of us with her unless someone plans for what happens when we lose.'
skillChecks.failure: Kael-Thun denies everything, becomes defensive, and avoids the party for the rest of the act. His secret remains hidden unless discovered by other means.

enemies: 3 Githyanki Warriors (CR 3, HP 49 each, AC 17 half plate; one carries 3 psionic charges — unstable crystals that deal 3d8 force damage in a 10-ft radius when detonated, DC 14 Dex save for half)
combatEncounters.tactics: The infiltrators fight in the Citadel's damaged corridors — narrow, cluttered with debris, and poorly lit where the crystal has gone dark. They use the environment expertly: one warrior engages in melee in the narrow corridor (only one party member can fight abreast), while the other two throw javelins from behind cover at 30 ft and 60 ft. If pressed, the warrior carrying the charges threatens to detonate them — the blast would collapse this section of corridor and potentially breach the wall into the Convergence Wound. This threat should create a tense negotiation moment: the party can try to disarm the situation (DC 16 Persuasion or DC 15 Intimidation to make the warrior surrender, or DC 17 Sleight of Hand to grab the charges). If the charges detonate, the blast deals 3d8 force damage to everyone within 10 ft and opens a 10-ft hole in the wall — through which shadow creatures begin emerging within 1d4 rounds. The infiltrators fight to the death only if cornered; they prefer to escape through the breach in the psychic ward and report to Kra'zith.
combatEncounters.terrain: Damaged Citadel corridor — 10 ft wide, 12 ft tall, with debris providing half cover at several points. The crystal walls have gone dark in this section (dim light only). A 5-ft wide crack in the floor opens onto the Astral void 30 ft below (DC 13 Dexterity save to avoid falling in if pushed; thought-based movement can arrest the fall with DC 14 Intelligence check). The concealed breach in the psychic ward is at one end of the corridor — the infiltrators' escape route.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This scene has two parallel threads that the party can pursue simultaneously or sequentially. The infiltrator thread is action-oriented: tracking, discovery, combat. The Kael-Thun thread is emotional: a sympathetic character making desperate choices out of a genuine desire to save lives. The two threads connect — Kael-Thun's negotiations gave the githyanki intelligence about the Citadel's weakest points, which the infiltrators are now exploiting. If the party discovers both threads, they face a meaningful choice: what to do with Kael-Thun? Options include turning him over to Zerith-Ka (who will be furious but fair — she exiles him from the order rather than executing him), keeping his secret and using his githyanki contact as a double agent (DC 18 Deception to feed false intelligence to Kra'zith through Kael-Thun), or forgiving him and letting him redeem himself in the final battle (if forgiven, Kael-Thun fights with desperate courage in Act 3 and may sacrifice himself to save a party member). There is no 'right' answer. The DM should present the situation honestly and let the party decide.
loot: Githyanki infiltrator equipment: 3 greatswords, 3 suits of half plate, 6 javelins, and a set of psionic charges (if captured intact: 3 charges, each deals 3d8 force damage in a 10-ft radius, DC 14 Dex save for half; can be detonated remotely by a character proficient in Arcana as a bonus action; single-use)

Infiltrator intelligence: a crystal tablet carried by the lead infiltrator containing Captain Kra'zith's assault plan — the timing, direction, and composition of the attack force; this intelligence is invaluable for preparing the Citadel's defense in the next scene
Breach access: the gap in the psychic ward, once discovered, can be sealed by a warden (takes 1 hour) or left open as a potential escape route or sally port for the party during the githyanki assault

scenes.name: The Siege of the Threshold
scenes.description: Captain Kra'zith launches the assault on the Threshold Citadel. A flotilla of githyanki warships — bone-white vessels bristling with warriors — emerges from the debris field and advances on the fortress from three directions simultaneously. The Citadel's remaining wardens rush to the walls, and Zerith-Ka channels her failing strength into the psychic defenses one last time. The party faces a choice: join the defense on the walls, where their combat strength is desperately needed, or use the chaos of the assault as cover to enter the Convergence Wound and seal the breach — the mission Zerith-Ka gave them. They cannot do both. This scene is designed as a decision point that defines the party's priorities and creates consequences that carry through the rest of the scenario.
scenes.readAloud: The alarm is not a sound — it is a feeling: a pulse of psychic urgency that jolts through your mind like a hand grabbing your shoulder, accompanied by Zerith-Ka's voice, calm even now, speaking directly into your thoughts. 'They are coming. All of you, to the walls.' You reach the central courtyard in time to see it. The Silver Wastes, normally a serene expanse of silver void and drifting debris, has become a war zone. Githyanki warships emerge from behind the debris clusters in a coordinated formation — six vessels, bone-white and bristling with armed figures, approaching from three directions to prevent the Citadel from concentrating its defense. The largest ship — a command vessel twice the size of the others, its prow carved into a snarling dragon skull — hangs in the void at the center of the formation, and standing on its deck, arms folded, silver armor gleaming, is a githyanki in a dragon-scale cloak who radiates authority the way the Convergence Wound radiates cold. Captain Kra'zith. Even at this distance, you can see the calculating intelligence in the githyanki captain's gaze as it sweeps across the Citadel's damaged walls, cataloguing weaknesses, measuring distances, deciding where to strike first. Beside you, Veth-Sora grips her staff with white-knuckled hands. Her face is set, her jaw tight, her dark eyes fixed on the approaching fleet. 'This is what we trained for,' she says, and her voice only shakes a little. 'This is what we—' She stops. Across the courtyard, Zerith-Ka has emerged from the Observatory. The ancient githzerai does not run — she walks with measured steps to the courtyard's center, raises her hands, and the Citadel's psychic defenses flare to life: a shimmering dome of telekinetic force that springs from the crystal walls and arches over the fortress like a soap bubble made of willpower. But you can see the cost. Zerith-Ka's face contorts with effort. The silver in her eyes blazes — and flickers. The dome shimmers, wavers, holds. But where the Convergence Wound touches the eastern wall, the dome has a gap: a dark crescent where the Shadowfell's corruption prevents the psychic energy from forming. The gap is thirty feet wide. Wide enough for a warship. Kra'zith has seen it too. The command vessel changes course, angling toward the gap. Zerith-Ka turns to you. 'The wound,' she says, and her voice is strained thin as wire. 'The wound must be sealed or the shield cannot hold. Go. Seal it. I will hold the walls as long as I can.' She pauses. 'As long as I can,' she repeats, and in those words you hear the truth she will not say: not long. Not long at all.'

skillChecks.success: The character assesses the githyanki formation and identifies a weakness: the two flanking ships are moving faster than the center group, creating a gap in the formation that will exist for approximately 2 minutes before the ships reach attack range. This window could allow a small team to slip past the fleet and approach from an unexpected angle — or provide timing intelligence for the Citadel's counterattack.
skillChecks.failure: The fleet appears to be in perfect formation. No weaknesses are visible.

skillChecks.success: The character senses that Zerith-Ka's psychic shield is not merely telekinetic force — she is burning her own life energy to power it. The shield will last approximately 30 minutes before her strength fails entirely. After that, the Citadel is open. This provides a hard deadline for sealing the Convergence Wound.
skillChecks.failure: The shield appears strong. No sense of its limitations.

skillChecks.success: The character reaches the eastern wing quickly, navigating the damaged corridors at speed and arriving at the Convergence Wound entrance with maximum time to complete the mission.
skillChecks.failure: A collapsed section of corridor forces a detour — the character loses 5 minutes and arrives at the wound with less time before the shield fails.

enemies: If the party joins the wall defense: 6 Githyanki Warriors (CR 3, HP 49 each, AC 17) attempting to breach through the gap in the psychic shield, led by a Githyanki Knight (Captain Kra'zith: CR 8, HP 91, AC 18 plate armor; armed with a silver greatsword +3 to hit over standard, and has Multiattack: 2 greatsword attacks per turn; can cast Misty Step at will and Plane Shift 1/day)

If the party enters the Convergence Wound during the assault (recommended path): 2 Githyanki Warriors (CR 3, HP 49 each) who breached through the wound's gap ahead of the main assault, plus the wound's own defenders (convergence wraiths and the shadow demon — see Convergence Wound encounters)
combatEncounters.tactics: Wall Defense: Kra'zith sends warriors in waves of 2 through the shield gap, testing the defenses, while positioning the command vessel to exploit any opening. Kra'zith personally enters combat only if the third wave fails — the captain fights with brutal efficiency, using Misty Step to flank defenders and targeting spellcasters first. If the defense holds for 20 minutes, Kra'zith withdraws — the captain is opportunistic, not suicidal, and will not throw lives away against a prepared defense. Wound Assault: The two githyanki warriors inside the wound are disoriented by the flickering physics and fighting defensively — they engaged convergence wraiths and lost, and are now cornered in a side chamber. They can be fought, bypassed, or even temporarily allied with against the wraiths (DC 16 Persuasion — they hate the shadow creatures more than they hate the party). This creates an interesting moral moment: working with githyanki against a common threat.
combatEncounters.terrain: Wall Defense: The Citadel's battlements provide three-quarters cover. The psychic shield blocks most approaches except the 30-ft gap at the eastern wing. The gap opens onto the Astral void — characters must use thought-based movement to fight in the gap itself. Falling off the battlements means falling into the void (thought-based movement to arrest, DC 14 Intelligence). Wound Assault: See Convergence Wound terrain features — flickering physics, planar overlay, shadow corruption.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This scene is designed to force a choice. The party cannot defend the walls AND seal the wound — there are not enough of them. Zerith-Ka makes the strategic calculus clear: the walls can hold temporarily, but only if the wound is sealed to close the gap in the shield. The wardens will fight on the walls; the party's unique Threadwalker abilities make them the only ones who can enter the wound and survive long enough to reach the epicenter. If the party splits (some on walls, some in the wound), that is a valid choice with valid consequences: the wall defenders fight fewer enemies but have less support, and the wound team faces its encounters with fewer resources. If the party insists on defending the walls first and entering the wound second, the shield fails after 30 minutes and the Citadel is breached — the wound must then be sealed under far worse conditions (additional githyanki warriors flood the corridors, convergence creatures grow bolder with the shield down). Captain Kra'zith should be established as a recurring antagonist — intelligent, pragmatic, and dangerous. If defeated here, the captain uses Plane Shift to escape, vowing to return. If the party does not engage Kra'zith directly, the captain's threat looms over future scenarios.
loot: Githyanki warrior equipment: greatswords, half plate, javelins (quantity depends on how many warriors the party defeats)

If Kra'zith is driven off or defeated: the captain's silver greatsword is left behind in the retreat — a +1 greatsword that deals an additional 1d6 psychic damage on a hit (requires attunement); if Kra'zith escapes, the sword goes with the captain

Warden gratitude: if the party's actions during the siege saved warden lives, Zerith-Ka formally inducts the party as honorary Astral Wardens, granting them the rank's privileges: free passage through any warden-held territory, access to warden supply caches scattered across the Astral Sea, and the right to call upon warden aid once per scenario (a warden NPC joins the party for one encounter)

acts.title: Act 3: Into the Wound
acts.description: The final act takes the party into the Convergence Wound — the hybrid zone of merged Astral and Shadowfell reality in the Citadel's eastern wing — to reach and stabilize the Confluence fragment at its epicenter. This is a dungeon crawl through a nightmare landscape where the rules change from room to room, where shadow and silver light coexist in sickening overlay, and where the enemies are born from the collision of two planes. The act builds from the disorienting outer corridors (flickering physics, echo corridors, shadow mastiff packs) through a gauntlet of convergence wraiths defending the approach, to the climactic confrontation at the epicenter: the Shadowfell Revenant that claims the fragment's warmth, the fragment itself pulsing with the memory of a unified multiverse, and the ritual to stabilize the breach while reality tears itself apart around the party. The act's resolution — sealing the Wound and calming the fragment — is not a victory but a reprieve. The fragment sleeps but does not die. The Wound closes but the scars remain. And from the Observatory, the party sees the truth: this was only one fragment. There are more. The campaign has begun.
objectives: Enter the Convergence Wound and navigate its hybrid reality
Fight through shadow creatures and convergence wraiths
Reach the epicenter and confront the Shadowfell Revenant
Stabilize the Confluence fragment through the sealing ritual
Return to the Observatory and receive the campaign's next objective

scenes.name: The Shadow Halls
scenes.description: The party enters the Convergence Wound through the breach in the eastern wing and immediately experiences the disorientation of existing in two planes simultaneously. The outer corridors of the Wound are a transitional zone where Astral and Shadowfell physics alternate unpredictably — gravity flickers on and off, light shifts between silver radiance and funereal grey, and the architecture is a nauseating double-image of crystalline thought-stone and Shadowfell basalt occupying the same space. Shadow mastiffs prowl these corridors, hunting by sound and movement in the flickering darkness, and echo corridors replay the deaths of wardens who fell when the breach first opened — shadowy figures that walk through walls, fall to invisible enemies, and scream in silence. The party must navigate this space, survive its predators, and push deeper toward the epicenter.
scenes.readAloud: You step through the breach and the world breaks in half. One eye sees the Citadel's corridor as it should be — crystalline walls glowing with soft silver light, the floor smooth and solid beneath your feet. The other eye sees something else: the same corridor, but wrong — the crystal replaced by rough black stone, the silver light drowned in grey twilight, the air heavy with the smell of ash and old grief. Both versions are real. Both versions occupy the same space. Your brain tries to reconcile the two images and fails, and for a lurching, nauseating moment you cannot tell which way is up, which wall is solid, or whether the floor beneath you is crystal or stone or nothing at all. Then the physics shift. Gravity — which had been absent in the Astral — slams back with Material Plane weight, and your knees buckle as your body remembers what it means to have mass. Your feet hit the floor — the stone floor, the Shadowfell version — and the impact is jarring and real. The silver light gutters. The corridor is dark now, lit only by a sickly grey glow that seems to come from the stones themselves, and in that glow you see the walls weep. Not water. Shadow. Black liquid that slides down the crystal-stone walls in slow rivulets, pooling on the floor in puddles that drink the light. The temperature has dropped thirty degrees. Your breath fogs. Your skin prickles. And somewhere in the darkness ahead — not far, not far enough — something breathes. Something with claws on stone. Something that smells warm blood in a cold place and begins to move.

skillChecks.success: The character maintains psychological coherence despite the dual-reality overlay. They can function normally in the Wound, perceiving both planes without confusion. Threadwalkers make this save with advantage.
skillChecks.failure: The character is overwhelmed by the dual-reality perception. Disadvantage on Charisma checks and saves (Shadowfell despair effect) for 30 minutes or until they leave the Wound.

skillChecks.success: The character hears the shadow mastiffs moving in the darkness — the click of claws, the huff of breath — and can pinpoint their positions despite the poor visibility. The party is not surprised and can prepare for the encounter.
skillChecks.failure: The ambient sounds of the Wound — the weeping walls, the grinding of stone, the whisper of shadow — mask the mastiffs' approach. They attack with surprise.

skillChecks.success: The character identifies the safest route through the Shadow Halls by following the sections where Astral physics dominate (silver light, no gravity) — these sections are less dangerous because the shadow creatures prefer Shadowfell-dominant areas. The route avoids one encounter.
skillChecks.failure: The character leads the party through a Shadowfell-dominant section where the darkness is thickest and the shadow creatures are most active.

skillChecks.success: The character recognizes the echo corridor phenomenon as a form of psychic imprint — the deaths of the wardens were so traumatic that they were burned into the Wound's fabric. The echoes are not ghosts and cannot interact with the living, but they carry information: watching an echo carefully (DC 13 Perception) reveals how the wardens died and, more importantly, what killed them — providing tactical intelligence about the deeper threats in the Wound.
skillChecks.failure: The echo corridors are terrifying and disorienting but yield no useful information.

enemies: 4 Shadow Mastiffs (CR 2, HP 33 each, AC 12; Shadow Blend: in dim light or darkness, the mastiff can use a bonus action to become invisible until it attacks or moves into bright light; Bite: +5 to hit, 2d6+3 piercing; if a target is hit, DC 13 Strength save or be knocked prone)
combatEncounters.tactics: The shadow mastiffs are pack hunters perfectly adapted to the Wound's environment. They use Shadow Blend to become invisible in the dim light of Shadowfell-dominant sections, then attack as a coordinated group: two mastiffs knock the target prone while the other two attack the prone target with advantage. They target isolated characters and avoid groups of three or more unless desperate. Light is their weakness — a torch, Light cantrip, or similar effect forces them to become visible and fight without their primary advantage. They retreat deeper into the Wound if more than half are killed, potentially leading the party into the convergence wraith territory ahead. During combat, the physics continue to flicker: at the DM's discretion, a gravity shift mid-fight can send combatants floating (Astral physics) or crashing down (Shadowfell physics), adding chaos to the encounter.
combatEncounters.terrain: Convergence Wound corridor — 15 ft wide, 12 ft tall. Dim light only (Shadowfell dominant in this section). Crystal-stone walls weep shadow liquid that creates difficult terrain in 5-ft patches. Physics flicker: roll 1d6 at the start of each round — on 1-3 Astral (no gravity, thought-based movement), on 4-6 Shadowfell (normal gravity, dim light). A gravity shift from Astral to Shadowfell drops floating creatures to the floor (DC 13 Dex save or fall prone and take 1d6 bludgeoning). Echo corridor intersections create visual noise — ghostly figures walking through walls may cause characters to mistake echoes for enemies (DC 12 Perception to distinguish).

scenes.roleplayNotes: The Shadow Halls should feel deeply wrong — not just dangerous but fundamentally broken. The dual-reality overlay is not a visual trick; it is the literal experience of existing in two places at once, and it should be described with visceral discomfort. The shadow mastiffs are not monsters in the traditional sense — they are Shadowfell predators that found themselves in a new hunting ground when the breach opened, and they have adapted with predatory efficiency. The echo corridors add emotional weight: the wardens who died here were people, with names and histories and relationships, and their deaths replay endlessly in the Wound's fabric. Veth-Sora, if she accompanies the party, recognizes some of the echoes — friends, mentors, training partners — and her reaction should be played for emotional impact. This is what the party is fighting to prevent from spreading.
loot: Shadow mastiff pelts: 4 pelts of supernatural shadow-stuff, worth 30 gp each to a collector of planar materials; a character proficient in Arcana can fashion one pelt into a Shadow Cloak during a long rest (grants advantage on Stealth checks in dim light or darkness, 1 use per day, lasts 1 hour)

Echo corridor discovery: if a character watches the echoes carefully (DC 13 Perception following a successful Religion check), they observe an echo-warden using a specific crystal key to seal a door deeper in the Wound — the door still exists, and finding the key (DC 14 Investigation in the echo-warden's quarters in the undamaged section of the Citadel) grants access to a shortcut that bypasses the convergence wraith gauntlet

Salvage from the Wound: scattered among the rubble are personal effects of fallen wardens — crystal focus objects worth 15 gp each (4 total), a scroll of Protection from Evil and Good, and a warden's journal describing the night the breach opened

scenes.name: The Wraith Gauntlet
scenes.description: Deeper in the Wound, the convergence wraiths have established territory in the corridors leading to the epicenter. These are not the scattered wraiths encountered in the Silver Wastes — this is a concentrated defense, as if the Wound itself has generated antibodies to protect its most vital organ. The wraiths emerge from the walls in waves, using the Shadowfell-dominant zones as staging areas and the flickering physics as a weapon, coordinating their attacks with the gravity shifts to maximum devastating effect. The party must fight through or find a way around the wraith gauntlet to reach the Breach Epicenter and the Shadowfell Revenant beyond.
scenes.readAloud: The corridor opens into a junction — four passages meeting at a central chamber that was once, judging by the shattered remnants of crystal benches and meditation cushions, a wardens' common room. Now it is a graveyard. The bodies of three githzerai wardens lie where they fell, frozen in death by the Shadowfell's cold. Their faces are masks of terror. Their crystal staffs are shattered. And around them, hovering in slow orbits like vultures circling carrion, are the wraiths. You have seen convergence wraiths before — in the Wastes, drifting like lost thoughts between the debris. These are different. These have fed. The Shadowfell energy pouring through the breach has gorged them, and they are larger, more defined, more present than their cousins in the open void. They have faces now — twisted, elongated faces that might once have been human or githzerai or something else entirely, stretched and distorted by the collision of planes until they are merely suggestions of features arranged in an expression of eternal, freezing hunger. They see you. The largest of them — a wraith that towers eight feet tall, its form trailing tendrils of shadow that lash the walls as it moves — opens its mouth. No sound emerges. But you feel it: a wave of cold that bypasses your skin and reaches directly into your chest, wrapping around your heart with fingers of ice. The wraith gestures, and the others spread out, blocking every passage, filling the junction with their shadows. The temperature plummets. Your breath freezes. The silver light dies. And in the darkness, the wraiths begin to advance.

skillChecks.success: The character identifies the wraiths' connection to the convergence breach — they are not independent creatures but extensions of the Wound itself, manifestations of the planar collision given form and hunger. They cannot be permanently destroyed while the breach remains open; destroyed wraiths reform within 1d4 hours. However, they can be disrupted by radiant or force damage, which scatters their essence for the full reformation period. This knowledge informs the party's strategy: fight through quickly rather than trying to clear the area.
skillChecks.failure: The wraiths appear to be standard undead, if unusually powerful. No deeper understanding of their nature.

skillChecks.success: The character identifies a structural weakness in the corridor ceiling — a section of crystal-stone that has been stressed by the convergence and could be collapsed with a targeted strike (DC 14 attack roll against AC 10) or spell. Collapsing the ceiling section blocks the main corridor with rubble, separating the wraith force and allowing the party to fight smaller groups sequentially.
skillChecks.failure: No environmental advantages are apparent. The party must fight the wraiths in the open junction.

skillChecks.success: If the party found the crystal key from the echo corridor discovery, they can access the shortcut that bypasses the wraith gauntlet entirely — a sealed maintenance corridor that runs parallel to the main passage and emerges beyond the wraith territory, within sight of the epicenter. This avoids the combat encounter completely but requires the party to have completed the Investigation check in the previous scene.
skillChecks.failure: The shortcut is sealed and the character cannot open it. The wraith gauntlet must be faced directly.

enemies: 5 Convergence Wraiths (CR 5, HP 67 each, AC 13; cold damage instead of necrotic; Life Drain: +6 to hit, 4d8+3 cold damage, target's HP max reduced by damage taken until long rest; creates a 5-ft Shadowfell overlay zone lasting 1 round; resistant to all damage except radiant and force while in a convergence fracture or Shadowfell-dominant zone)

1 Greater Convergence Wraith (use Wraith stats with HP 100, AC 14; all standard wraith abilities plus: Convergence Wail — recharge 5-6, 30-ft cone, DC 15 Constitution save or 4d8 cold damage and speed reduced to 0 until end of next turn; can command lesser wraiths to focus attacks on a single target as a bonus action)
combatEncounters.tactics: The wraiths fight in the junction, using it as a kill zone. The greater wraith hangs back, using Convergence Wail to pin down the party while the lesser wraiths swarm forward with Life Drain attacks. The wraiths coordinate with the physics flickers: during Shadowfell-dominant rounds, they are in their element (resistance to most damage) and attack aggressively; during Astral-dominant rounds, they retreat into the walls and corridors, using their incorporeal movement to avoid damage. The Shadowfell overlay zones created by Life Drain chain together, building expanding areas of darkness that favor the wraiths. The party must use radiant and force damage aggressively — these bypass the wraiths' resistance regardless of the current physics state. If the party uses the ceiling collapse tactic, the wraith force is divided: 3 wraiths on one side, 2 wraiths and the greater wraith on the other, fought separately. If the party has the crystal key shortcut, this encounter is bypassed entirely.
combatEncounters.terrain: Junction chamber — 30 ft x 30 ft central room with four 10-ft wide corridors branching off. Dim light (Shadowfell dominant). The dead wardens' bodies and shattered crystal create difficult terrain in the center. Physics flicker: roll 1d6 each round (1-3 Astral, 4-6 Shadowfell). The ceiling is 15 ft high and partially collapsed in two corners, creating rubble piles that provide half cover. The Shadowfell overlay zones from Life Drain attacks accumulate, potentially covering the entire junction in darkness within 3-4 rounds if the party does not advance past the wraiths quickly.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This is the scenario's most intense combat encounter, designed to feel like a desperate push through enemy territory with a ticking clock (Zerith-Ka's shield failing outside). The wraiths should be terrifying — not because they are individually overwhelming but because they keep coming, because the darkness keeps spreading, and because every moment spent fighting them is a moment the shield outside grows weaker. The greater wraith's Convergence Wail should be a dramatic threat that forces the party to adapt tactically: it punishes clustering but the wraiths also punish isolation. The ideal approach is aggressive forward movement — fight through, not fight to clear — which reinforces the scenario's urgency. If Veth-Sora is present, she fights beside the party with desperate courage but is clearly outmatched; protecting her becomes an additional objective that adds emotional stakes. If the party uses the shortcut, they bypass the combat but miss the dramatic intensity and the loot — a valid trade-off that rewards thorough exploration in the previous scene.
loot: Greater convergence wraith essence: when the greater wraith is destroyed, it collapses into a crystal of frozen shadow the size of a fist, pulsing with cold energy; this is a Shard of Convergence — an uncommon wondrous item that can be attuned to grant resistance to cold damage permanently (requires attunement); alternatively, it can be consumed to cast Dispel Magic at 5th level once, targeting planar effects (after which it is destroyed)

Fallen warden equipment: from the three dead wardens in the junction — 3 crystalline staffs (broken but repairable: DC 15 Arcana during a long rest restores one staff as a +1 quarterstaff that deals an additional 1d4 psychic damage), 3 Warden's Sigils, and 3 sets of Warden's Robes

Environmental salvage: the convergence has fused Astral and Shadowfell materials in the junction walls; DC 16 Investigation to find a palm-sized piece of merged crystal-shadow worth 100 gp to a planar scholar; it also functions as a spellcasting focus that adds +1 to the DC of spells from the Necromancy school

scenes.name: The Epicenter
scenes.description: The climax of the scenario. The party reaches the epicenter of the Convergence Wound — the chamber where the Confluence fragment's awakening tore reality apart and the Shadowfell first bled into the Astral Sea. Here the dual-reality overlay is total: every surface, every sound, every sensation exists in two states simultaneously, and the fragment itself — a sphere of white-gold light embedded in a mass of merged crystal and basalt — pulses with the memory of a unified multiverse, beautiful and terrible in equal measure. The Shadowfell Revenant occupies the chamber, drawn to the fragment's warmth, and it will not surrender its only source of light and heat willingly. The party must confront the Revenant, reach the fragment, and perform the stabilization ritual — a one-minute psychic-arcane procedure during which the ritualist is utterly vulnerable — while the Wound fights to remain open and the remnants of the wraith force press in from behind.
scenes.readAloud: The corridor ends. The wall ahead has been torn away — not collapsed, not eroded, but torn, as if two enormous hands gripped the crystal-stone on either side and pulled in different directions until reality split down the middle. Through the ragged gap, you see the epicenter. It is a chamber that should not exist. The crystal meditation room that was here — you can see its ghost, its Astral reflection, luminous walls and smooth floor and the quiet beauty of githzerai architecture — has been fused with a Shadowfell crypt. Grey stone has grown through the crystal like bone through flesh. Iron sconces trail green flame where crystal light fixtures once glowed. A floor of smooth thought-stone is split by flagstones of mortuary granite, and in the cracks between the two surfaces, darkness pools like blood. And at the center of this impossible space, half-embedded in a pillar of merged materials where crystal meets basalt, the Confluence fragment burns. It is the size of a human head — a perfect sphere of white-gold light that radiates warmth in a place of cold, life in a place of death, unity in a place of fracture. Looking at it is like looking at a sunrise through stained glass: the light carries color and meaning and memory, and the memory it carries is vast — the memory of a time before separation, before boundaries, before the loneliness of individual existence. It is heartbreaking. It is terrifying. It is the most beautiful thing you have ever seen. The fragment pulses, and with each pulse the Wound expands — you can see the walls of the chamber ripple outward, the merged reality growing an inch with each heartbeat of that golden light. And standing between you and the fragment, one hand resting on the pillar as if drawing warmth from a hearth, is the Revenant. It was human, once. Maybe. The tattered robes, the skeletal hands, the hollow pits where eyes once burned — these are human features, or a memory of them. But the Shadowfell has refined this creature the way a glacier refines a mountain: stripping away everything soft, everything living, leaving only the essential shape of hunger and cold. It turns its hollow gaze toward you, and you feel the weight of its attention like a hand pressing on your chest. 'More warmth,' it says, and its voice is the sound of wind through a crypt. 'More light. More life in this dead place.' It looks at the fragment, then at you, and in the empty pits of its eyes something flickers — not malice, not hunger, but something older and sadder. Recognition. 'You have come to take it from me,' the Revenant says. 'The only warm thing in all the grey. The only light in all the dark.' It straightens to its full height — seven feet of shadow and bone and tattered robes — and the temperature drops so low that frost crystals form on your armor. 'I cannot allow that,' it says. 'I am sorry. But I have been cold for so very, very long.'

skillChecks.success: The character appeals to the Revenant's lost humanity — addressing it by its former identity (if the journal fragment was found) or simply recognizing its pain as something more than monstrous hunger. The Revenant pauses. 'You... see me,' it says, with something like wonder. 'Not the dead thing. The person I was.' It agrees to step away from the fragment — not willingly, but with the desperate dignity of someone surrendering the only thing that makes existence bearable. It asks for one thing in return: 'Remember me. Remember that I was warm, once. That I was alive. That I chose to let go.' It retreats to the chamber's edge and watches as the party works, weeping shadow-tears that freeze before they fall.
skillChecks.failure: The Revenant cannot be reached. Its hunger for warmth overwhelms whatever humanity remains. Combat begins.

skillChecks.success: The character performs the stabilization ritual — a one-minute procedure of psychic-arcane channeling that calms the fragment without destroying it, like soothing a crying child. The fragment's pulse slows, its light dims to a gentle glow, and the Wound begins to close: the merged surfaces separate, the Shadowfell bleeds away, and the crystal reasserts itself. The process takes 10 minutes after the ritual completes, and during that time the chamber is wracked with tremors as reality reconfigures. When it is done, the eastern wing is still damaged — scarred and dark where the Wound was — but the breach is sealed. The Shadowfell is gone. The fragment sleeps.
skillChecks.failure: The ritual falters — the character's concentration breaks as the fragment pulses with overwhelming memory. The character takes 2d8 psychic damage and must start the ritual over. A second failure means the ritual requires two characters working in tandem (both must succeed on DC 16 Arcana) or the use of the partial formula from the Revenant's journal (grants advantage on the check).

skillChecks.success: The character resists the fragment's radiant energy while performing the ritual, maintaining their position within the 10-ft proximity zone without taking damage.
skillChecks.failure: The character takes 2d8 radiant damage from the fragment's raw planar energy at the start of the ritual. This damage repeats if the ritual must be restarted.

skillChecks.success: During or after the ritual, the character perceives the fragment's nature: it is not a weapon or a bomb or a piece of machinery. It is a memory — a fragment of consciousness that remembers being part of everything. Its awakening is not an attack but a cry of recognition, like a child who sees a parent's face after years of separation. This understanding fundamentally reframes the Convergence crisis and provides crucial philosophical context for the campaign.
skillChecks.failure: The fragment is stabilized but its nature remains mysterious — merely a dangerous piece of planar energy that needed to be contained.

enemies: The Shadowfell Revenant (CR 5, HP 136, AC 13; Slam: +7 to hit, 2d8+3 bludgeoning; Vengeful Glare: target within 30 ft, DC 15 Wisdom save or frightened for 1 minute; Shadowfell Wail: recharge 5-6, 30-ft cone, DC 15 Constitution save or 4d8 necrotic damage and frightened for 1 minute; Rejuvenation: if destroyed while the fragment is active, the Revenant reforms in 24 hours; this rejuvenation ends when the fragment is stabilized)

2 Convergence Wraiths (CR 5, HP 67 each, AC 13 — these emerge from the walls 3 rounds into combat, representing the Wound's 'immune response' to the party's intrusion; they target the character closest to the fragment)
combatEncounters.tactics: The Revenant fights defensively near the fragment, positioning itself between the party and the sphere of light. It uses Shadowfell Wail to push the party back, then follows up with Vengeful Glare on anyone who approaches within 30 ft. It fights with desperate ferocity but not mindless aggression — it uses the terrain (the merged crystal-basalt pillar provides half cover, the flickering physics create unpredictable gravity shifts) and retreats when badly hurt, using its proximity to the fragment to heal (it regains 10 HP at the start of each turn while within 10 ft of the active fragment). The convergence wraiths that emerge at round 3 add pressure: they target the character closest to the fragment, trying to prevent the ritual from being performed. If the Revenant is reduced to 0 HP, it collapses but does not die — it begins reforming (visible as shadow-stuff coalescing) and will return to full HP in 1d4 minutes unless the fragment is stabilized first. This creates the scenario's central tactical challenge: someone must keep the Revenant occupied while someone else performs the ritual. The ritual takes 1 minute (10 rounds) and requires concentration — taking damage forces a DC 14 Constitution save to maintain concentration, as if concentrating on a spell.
combatEncounters.terrain: Epicenter chamber — roughly 40 ft x 40 ft, irregular shape. The merged crystal-basalt pillar occupies the center, with the fragment embedded at chest height. The floor is split between crystal and flagstone with darkness pooling in the cracks (difficult terrain in a patchwork pattern). Physics flicker: roll 1d6 each round (1-3 Astral, 4-6 Shadowfell). The fragment's radiance creates a 10-ft bright light radius and 20-ft dim light radius — within bright light, the wraiths lose their damage resistance. The chamber has two exits: the corridor the party entered from and a collapsed section of wall that opens onto the Astral void (visible through the remaining crystal). Shadow corruption covers the walls, reducing healing by half in the chamber. Temperature is near freezing; nonmagical water and liquids freeze within minutes.

scenes.roleplayNotes: This is the scenario's emotional and dramatic climax, and it should be played for maximum impact on both levels. Mechanically, the fight is a complex tactical challenge: the Revenant's regeneration near the fragment means it cannot be simply killed — it must be managed while the ritual is performed. The convergence wraiths add time pressure. The flickering physics add chaos. And the ritualist is vulnerable for 10 full rounds. Emotionally, the scene is about confronting something that is not purely evil — the Revenant is a tragic figure drawn to the only warmth in an eternity of cold, and the fragment is not a bomb but a memory of unity that aches with loneliness. The party can fight their way through on pure combat prowess, but the most satisfying resolution involves understanding: negotiating with the Revenant (requiring the journal fragment and a high Persuasion), comprehending the fragment's nature (the Insight check), and stabilizing it with compassion rather than force. If the Revenant is negotiated with rather than destroyed, it watches the party seal the Wound and, as the Shadowfell recedes, it begins to dissolve — the warmth it needed is leaving with the fragment's calming. In its final moments, it whispers its name (the one from the journal, if found) and thanks the party for seeing the person it was. Then it is gone. This should be a moment of genuine sadness.
loot: The Revenant's journal fragment (if not already found): contains the partial formula that grants advantage on the stabilization ritual check; also contains the Revenant's name and a partial account of their life — a wizard who studied the planes and died in the Shadowfell; worth keeping as a story artifact

Fragment Resonance: each character who participated in the stabilization ritual (or who touched the fragment) gains a permanent minor benefit — their silver compass now shows faint thread-lines connecting convergence zones, providing advantage on Arcana checks to navigate between zones; additionally, they can sense convergence breaches within 1 mile (they feel a chill and the compass needle trembles)
Convergence Shard (from the greater wraith, if fought in this scene or the previous one): see previous scene's loot description

Warden's Gratitude Cache: after the Wound is sealed, Zerith-Ka opens a sealed vault in the Citadel's armory containing equipment prepared for the Threadwalkers' mission — each party member receives one item of their choice from the following: a Cloak of Protection, Boots of Elvenkind, Goggles of Night, a Periapt of Wound Closure, or a Bag of Holding; additionally, the party receives a communal chest containing 500 gp in mixed Astral currency (planar trade gems, githzerai meditation crystals, and raw thought-crystal worth standard gold value)
